role: Read-only mathematical analysis of the existing EOS estimator; not a replacement method specification, candidate, or new acceptance gate
assumptions: Preserve the accepted idealization: exact model-estimated token counterfactual values are the corresponding real-world variable values.
At a fixed prefix h, p_a(Y) is the factual outcome law and q(Y|h) is the same deletion reference law across choices of the actual token a.
The reference law is covered by each factual outcome law used in the importance-sampling identity, and the expectations being asserted exist.
The derivation applies to the raw source-token estimator before finite-batch whitening and PPO clipping; self-target boundary semantics remain as fixed in PLAN.md.

expected_gradient_property.conceptual_reference_return: B_del(h)=sum_Y r(Y)*q(Y|h); no B module or extra computation is introduced
expected_gradient_property.scope: Sampling-policy, unclipped expected score-function gradient, with the same state/token weights. This is not equality of every sampled coefficient or of finite-batch whitened/clipped PPO updates.
expected_gradient_property.action_comparison: At the same prefix, differences of conditional expected deletion advantages equal differences of Q_pi values because the same B_del is subtracted.
expected_gradient_property.exact_PPO_advantage_condition: Conditional mean equals Q_pi-V_pi when B_del(h)=V_pi(h). Gradient equivalence itself does not require this additional equality.

optimality_scope.conclusion: Neither unbiased expected-gradient equivalence nor an exact deletion reference implies minimum gradient variance.
optimality_scope.ordinary_scalar_baseline_comparison: For a single fixed-prefix gradient term z(a)*(G-b(h)), z=grad log pi, the state-only scalar baseline minimizing conditional trace covariance is b_star=E[||z||^2*G|h]/E[||z||^2|h], when these second moments exist and the denominator is positive.
optimality_scope.value_function_property: V_pi=E[G|h] minimizes unweighted conditional squared return-prediction error. This objective differs from score-weighted gradient variance.
optimality_scope.comparison_limit: The scalar-baseline formula is not an optimizer for the outcome-dependent importance estimator above, full trajectory covariance, or the PPO clipped loss. It explains why no general variance-optimality theorem follows from the expected-gradient identity.
optimality_scope.implementation_change: None. No learned critic, alternative reference, extra reference-token sampling, or new baseline module is proposed.

approximation_bias_analysis.gradient_error: Let C_i be the implemented raw DT credit and C_i_exact the accepted exact deletion credit on the same rollout. The raw gradient bias is E[sum_i grad log pi(a_i|h_i)*(C_i-C_i_exact)]. Zero mean credit error or conserved total credit alone does not make this score-weighted expectation vanish.
approximation_bias_analysis.finite_horizon_scope: Only the actual finite task horizon is considered. An L-step Bellman return with the correct terminal bootstrap preserves the corresponding conditional return expectation. Bootstrap error enters as gamma^L times the terminal value error; finite-horizon truncation by itself is not a universal optimal-policy guarantee. This is distinct from an action-correlated credit-estimation error.
approximation_bias_analysis.unbiased_residual_identity_for_research: For any fixed rollout and approximate C_i, select source positions with known positive inclusion probabilities eta_i, without looking at their unqueried exact deletion values. Define C_i_corrected=C_i+I_i/eta_i*(C_i_exact-C_i). Then E_selection[C_i_corrected|rollout]=C_i_exact. Together with the existing idealized deletion-gradient identity this removes approximation bias from the raw expected score gradient, while retaining dense DT information as a model-assisted approximation.
approximation_bias_analysis.residual_variance: For each fixed rollout and token, Var_selection(C_i_corrected)=(1/eta_i-1)*(C_i_exact-C_i)^2. Source-selection correlations also affect the full gradient variance. Rare large residuals can make this construction unsuitable even though its expectation is correct.
approximation_bias_analysis.cost_and_status: This identity needs some actual single-deletion measurements; it is not a free normalization of the present DT vector. No query budget, training candidate, extra forward calls, loss change, or deployment was selected. The existing probability sample supports read-only study of residuals, not a claim that this construction has been accepted or is efficient.
approximation_bias_analysis.reference_scope: Replacing C_i_exact with a numerical native measurement corrects toward that measurement; its model/numerical error remains separately recorded. Idealized world equivalence follows only under the accepted exact-token-value premise and the existing reference conditions.
approximation_bias_analysis.PPO_scope: The unbiasedness identity is for raw credit and its linear score gradient. Subsequent finite-batch whitening and clipping retain their existing nonlinear effects; this is not a proof of equality of clipped PPO updates.

negative_tail_interpretation.exact_case: With positive reward, an exact ratio q(Y|h)/p_a(Y)>1 gives negative sampled credit: the selected token suppresses this realized rewarded outcome relative to deletion. This does not alone establish that its conditional expected return is worse.
negative_tail_interpretation.large_values: Exact importance ratios can be large when the observed outcome is rare under the factual action. A large negative sample is not by itself proof of estimation error or of minimum variance.
negative_tail_interpretation.error_propagation: For epsilon=d_DT-d_true, A_DT-A_true=-r*exp(-d_true)*(exp(-epsilon)-1). Negative d error is amplified by the exponential.
negative_tail_interpretation.conditional_bias_mechanism: Holding r>0 and d_true fixed, conditionally zero-mean epsilon implies a nonpositive expected credit error by Jensen when the required expectations exist. This is a possible mechanism, not an empirical claim that the observed prediction-selected tail proves an all-token bias.

primary_sources.title: Hindsight Credit Assignment
primary_sources.supports: The hindsight likelihood-ratio value/advantage identity under the paper's coverage assumption.
primary_sources.does_not_claim: The paper uses a policy-marginal reference. The EOS deletion reference's action-independent-baseline extension above is our explicit derivation; the paper does not establish EOS deletion variance optimality.

primary_sources.title: Variance Reduction Techniques for Gradient Estimates in Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.supports: Score-weighted variance-optimal baselines and the distinction between a true value function and a variance-optimal gradient baseline.
primary_sources.derivation_scope: The conditional vector-norm single-term formula recorded above is an explicit elementary minimization, not a claim that the paper proves a full DT/PPO optimum.

primary_sources.title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
primary_sources.location: Section 3, Proposition 1 and the k-step advantage construction
primary_sources.supports: Distinguishing return/advantage-estimation bias, bootstrapped value accuracy, and the policy-gradient expectation. The elementary random-source residual identity above is our own explicit conditioning argument, not a theorem attributed to GAE.

primary_sources.title: Doob conditional-expectation martingale explanation by Scott Sheffield
primary_sources.location: page 1, lines explaining increasing-information conditional expectations
primary_sources.supports: M_k=E[G|F_k] is a martingale. The finite telescoping token/action accounting above is our explicit specialization.

primary_sources.title: RUDDER: Return Decomposition for Delayed Rewards
primary_sources.supports: Return-equivalent reward redistribution; its optimality is defined by zero expected future redistributed reward, with consecutive Q differences. This is a related formal allocation definition, not a claim that raw DT deletion effects or our present implementation satisfy it.

sequential_credit_and_overlap.role: Analysis of the user question, not an accepted alternative implementation or a new plan
sequential_credit_and_overlap.horizon: Only the fixed finite task horizon. G=sum of rewards within that horizon; current gamma=1.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.formal_PPO_token_coefficient: C_star(h,a)=E[G|h,a]-E[G|h]=Q_pi(h,a)-V_pi(h), with already collected rewards cancelling in the difference.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.uniqueness: For each reachable prefix h, require C(h,a)-C(h,b)=Q_pi(h,a)-Q_pi(h,b) for supported actions, and E_pi[C(h,a)|h]=0. These two conditions imply uniquely C=Q_pi-V_pi, up to null-probability events.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.causal_order: The next token conditions on the actual earlier token. A change already included in that prefix value is not added again; the next coefficient measures its own remaining conditional deviation.

example.assumption: No intervening observation or reward in this illustration; future policy is included in each expectation.

sequential_credit_and_overlap.martingale_statement: With the natural chronological information filtration F_k and M_k=E[G|F_k], D_k=M_{k+1}-M_k has E[D_k|F_k]=0 and sum_k D_k=G-E[G|F_0] when the terminal sigma-field reveals G. An action reveal before external randomness has D=Q-V. Observations/reward reveals supply other conditional innovations, are not policy actions, and receive no actor loss. This is a formal accounting identity, not observation-credit routing.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.deletion_overlap: Separate exact single-token total deletion effects are contrasts from different interventions. They can overlap and need not sum to one conserved reward. This is not a contradiction of exact counterfactual values. Adding a downstream total effect to an upstream effect that already includes it is double counting if presented as one disjoint allocation.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.policy_gradient: The training target is E[sum_i z_i C_i]=E[sum_i z_i A_pi_i], where z_i=grad log pi(a_i|h_i). This is not a requirement that sum_i C_i equal terminal reward. Reusing a realized return with different token scores is not itself double counting.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.EOS_reference_relation: Under the existing common-reference and coverage assumptions, bar_C_del(h,a)=E[C_del|h,a]=Q_pi(h,a)-B_del(h). Then bar_C_del(h,a)-E_pi[bar_C_del(h,a)|h]=Q_pi(h,a)-V_pi(h). This identifies the baseline offset mathematically; it is not an instruction to add a learned critic, reference-token sampling, per-prefix LLM queries, or trajectory-mean substitution.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.unbiased_error_requirement: For approximate raw credit C_i=C_exact_i+e_i, the gradient error is E[sum_i z_i e_i]. Conservation, zero average e, or tokenwise sign accuracy alone do not establish this quantity is zero.
sequential_credit_and_overlap.implementation: No changes to DT/Q/V/A/whitening/PPO, no new candidate, no deployment or formal restart.
